title: CS Fundamentals — Systems, Complexity & Networks
description: Broad CS fundamentals: complexity, memory hierarchy, concurrency, OS, networking, and distributed-systems trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Binary search over a sorted array of n elements has worst-case time complexity:
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the search space, giving logarithmic time.

questions.prompt: Within a single process, multiple threads share which of the following?

options: The address space and heap (but each has its own stack)

questions.explanation: Threads share the process's address space and heap; each thread keeps its own stack and registers.

questions.prompt: TCP provides ordered, reliable byte-stream delivery, whereas UDP does not guarantee ordering or delivery.
questions.explanation: TCP adds sequencing, acknowledgements, and retransmission; UDP is a thin, best-effort datagram layer.

questions.prompt: Under the CAP theorem, during a network partition a distributed system must trade off between:
questions.explanation: When partitioned (P is unavoidable), you choose C or A — reject/stall to stay consistent, or answer possibly-stale to stay available.

questions.prompt: The smallest, fastest CPU cache level nearest the core is named ___.
questions.explanation: L1 is fastest/smallest, then L2, then a larger shared L3 — the memory hierarchy trades size for speed.

questions.prompt: Virtual-to-physical address translation is performed using a:
questions.explanation: The OS maintains page tables; the TLB caches recent translations to avoid repeated walks.

questions.prompt: Deadlock requires all four Coffman conditions. Which is one of them?
questions.explanation: Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait must all hold; breaking any one prevents deadlock.

questions.prompt: On-disk database indexes are usually B-trees / B+ trees because they:

options: Have high fan-out and shallow depth, minimizing disk seeks
Use the least RAM of any structure
Are simpler than a linked list

questions.explanation: High branching keeps the tree shallow, so a lookup touches few pages — ideal when each page access is a slow seek.

questions.prompt: Two's complement is the standard binary encoding for signed integers on modern CPUs.
questions.explanation: Two's complement gives a single zero and lets the same adder handle signed and unsigned addition.

questions.prompt: Explain why adding more threads can make a program slower rather than faster, citing at least two causes.

payload.rubric: Names ≥2 of: lock contention, context-switch/scheduling overhead, cache-line/false sharing, Amdahl's law limiting the serial fraction, memory-bandwidth saturation.
